2. Verified Current State
The following was confirmed by direct inspection of the two repositories prior to writing this brief.
2.1 Landing Page Repository (ai-attendance-project-landing)
Flask application with a single route (“/”) that renders one Jinja2 template, index.html.

Contains a vercel.json — deployed on Vercel.
Folders: templates/ and static/.
2.2 Main Application Repository (ai-attendance-project-app)
Streamlit application (not a client/server SPA — Streamlit owns rendering, routing, and state in one Python process).

Entry point app.py switches between home_screen, teacher_screen, and student_screen based on st.session_state['login_type'], and opens a dialog_auto_enroll component when a join-code query parameter i

Face recognition: dlib-bin, face_recognition_models, scikit-learn.

Voice recognition: resemblyzer and librosa are present — the app appears to support voice-embedding-based identification alongside face recognition. This was not mentioned in prior feature description
Password hashing: bcrypt. QR code generation: segno.
App display name: “SnapClass — Making Attendance faster using AI.”

3. Non-Negotiable Guardrails
These constraints apply to every phase below. If a requested feature genuinely cannot be built within them, stop and flag it instead of silently swapping technology.
Keep Streamlit as the application framework for the main app. Do not migrate to React/Next.js/Django/FastAPI.
Keep Flask + Jinja2 + static assets for the landing page. Do not migrate to a JS framework or SSG.
Keep Supabase as the database and auth/storage backend. Do not introduce a second database or a custom ORM layer.
Keep face_recognition / dlib as the face-recognition engine, and resemblyzer / librosa as the voice engine, unless a version bump is required for compatibility.
Keep bcrypt for password hashing and segno for QR generation.
Keep the Vercel deployment target for the landing page.
No secrets, API keys, or Supabase service-role keys are ever hard-coded — use environment variables and confirm a .env.example exists.
Every change must leave the app runnable. No “big bang” rewrites — refactor in place, one reviewable change at a time.
4. Project Goal
Redesign SnapClass into a premium-feeling product — visually on par with Linear, Vercel, Stripe, Notion, Clerk, and Supabase — without changing the underlying technology choices. The work spans three
Track A — Documentation: reverse-engineer and document the real architecture.
Track B — UI/UX redesign: modern visual language across both repos, applied within Streamlit's and Flask/Jinja's actual rendering models.
Track C — Feature & quality improvements: fill genuine gaps (analytics, exports, audit trail, etc.) and harden security/performance.

7. Phase 3 — UI/UX Redesign Direction

Streamlit and static Jinja/HTML both allow real custom styling — use component-level CSS injection (st.markdown with unsafe_allow_html, or a shared assets/styles.css) rather than fighting the framewor
7.1 Visual language
Neutral dark-charcoal or off-white base, one confident accent color, generous whitespace — avoid default Streamlit widget chrome wherever it reads as generic.
Card-based layout for attendance lists, teacher rosters, and student profiles; consistent corner radius and shadow scale.
Typography: one display face for headings, one readable body face; consistent type scale across both repos.
Subtle glassmorphism on modal/dialog surfaces (the auto-enroll dialog is a good candidate) — used sparingly, not on every panel.
Dark mode as a real toggle, not just “browser default,” persisted per user session.
7.2 States to design explicitly
Loading states for face-scan capture, voice-embedding processing, and Supabase round-trips (skeletons/spinners, not blank screens).
Empty states for “no attendance yet,” “no students enrolled,” “no classes today.”
Error states for camera/mic permission denial, failed recognition match, and Supabase connectivity failure — human-readable, actionable messages.
7.3 Screens in scope
Landing page (Flask): hero, feature highlights, how-it-works, CTA into the app.
Home / login screen
Teacher dashboard: class roster, live attendance, analytics
Student screen: join flow, personal attendance history
Auto-enroll dialog (face + voice capture)

9. Phase 5 — Security & Performance Pass
Security
Confirm no Supabase service-role key is used client-side; only the anon/public key with RLS enforced.
Validate and sanitize any join-code / query-param input before use.
Rate-limit or debounce repeated face/voice recognition attempts.
Confirm bcrypt cost factor is adequate; confirm no plaintext credentials in logs.
Performance
Cache expensive operations (face-encoding model load, Supabase reference data) with st.cache_resource / st.cache_data.
Avoid recomputation on every Streamlit rerun — audit for state that should live in st.session_state instead of being recalculated.
Compress/resize captured images before encoding; check audio clip length before running resemblyzer.
